Optimal.Notes: Native resolution at medium settings delivers a sharp, smooth experience with good battery life for extended city-building sessions. If fps dips below 50 on a large late-game kingdom, reduce Shadow Quality and Terrain Detail to Low.

profiles.Summary: Kingdoms and Castles is a lightweight indie city-builder with modest PC requirements well below the Steam Deck's capabilities, so it runs comfortably at 60 fps or higher even on large maps. No Deck-specific reports were found, but the low system requirements and Verified status strongly suggest a smooth, trouble-free experience.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck–specific player reports were found; profiles are estimated from the game's modest PC requirements (GTX 660-class recommended, well below the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU) and its Verified/Platinum status. On your first run, check fps on a large late-game map — if the simulation causes CPU-side dips, lower the frame cap rather than GPU settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 5 W TDP and a reduced render resolution the Deck barely breaks a sweat on this lightweight city-builder, giving excellent battery life even on large kingdoms. FSR upscaling keeps the image acceptable at 40 fps; drop to 30 fps cap if late-game simulation causes dips.

KnownIssues: Late-game large kingdoms with many simulated villagers and resources may cause CPU-side slowdowns as the simulation scales up.
No native Linux build — runs via Proton, though Verified status and platinum ProtonDB rating indicate no major issues.
UI text may be small at 1280x800 on the Deck screen in some menus.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Deck's GPU is far above this game's recommended spec, so high settings at 90 Hz is realistic on early-to-mid game maps. Very large late-game kingdoms may become CPU-bound by simulation load, dropping to the 50-60 fps range regardless of GPU settings.
